topic: Computational methods for rigorous volume computation of semialgebraic sets — toolbox for computing P(random polynomial with i.i.d. uniform coefficients has all real roots) = normalized volume of the discriminant-nonnegative region

findings.claim: Henrion, Lasserre, Savorgnan (SIAM Review 51(4):722-743, 2009) 'Approximate Volume and Integration for Basic Semialgebraic Sets' generates a sequence converging to the volume of a compact basic semialgebraic set K in R^n, obtained from optimal values of a hierarchy of semidefinite (or linear) programs; it also approximates every finite vector of moments of the uniform probability measure on K, hence integrals of arbitrary polynomials over K.
findings.source: D. Henrion, J. B. Lasserre, C. Savorgnan, 'Approximate Volume and Integration for Basic Semialgebraic Sets', SIAM Review 51(4):722-743, 2009. https://researchr.org/publication/HenrionLS09
findings.notes: Abstract content confirmed via multiple secondary listings. This is the foundational paper for topic 1. Finite-order bounds are one-sided (upper bounds on volume in exact arithmetic), but SDPs are solved in floating point, so finite-order output is NOT a rigorous certificate without extra rounding/validation work.

findings.claim: Korda-Henrion prove the asymptotic convergence rate of the moment-SOS volume hierarchy is at least O(1/log log d) in d = polynomial degree. Exact abstract sentence: 'We show that the asymptotic rate of this convergence is at least O(1/ log log d).'
findings.source: M. Korda, D. Henrion, 'Convergence rates of moment-sum-of-squares hierarchies for volume approximation of semialgebraic sets', Optimization Letters 12 (2018); arXiv:1612.04146. https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.04146
findings.notes: Quoted directly from arXiv abstract. Secondary sources (Springer page summary) add: rate improves to O(1/log d) when the set is defined by a single polynomial inequality — that refinement is 'likely' (not seen in the primary abstract). Consequence for our project: convergence in degree is extremely slow in theory; only 2-4 digits are realistic without Stokes constraints.

findings.claim: Tacchi, Lasserre, Henrion ('Stokes, Gibbs and Volume Computation of Semi-Algebraic Sets', Discrete & Computational Geometry, 2023; arXiv:2009.12139) show the plain hierarchy suffers a Gibbs phenomenon (approximating a discontinuous indicator by polynomials) causing slow convergence; adding linear moment constraints derived from Stokes' theorem makes the dual LP have a CONTINUOUS optimal solution, eliminating Gibbs and drastically accelerating convergence. Measured examples (Matlab + YALMIP SOS parser + GloptiPoly moment parser + MOSEK): (a) disk of radius 1/2 inside unit disk, n=2, degree d=16: without Stokes estimate 1.1626 (47.8% error vs true pi/4 ~ 0.7854), with Stokes 0.7870 (0.2% error); (b) 3D ball radius 3/4: d=8 error 57% (0.16 s) without Stokes vs 1.0% (0.44 s) with; d=12: 47% (1.97 s) vs 0.0% (4.63 s); (c) l4-ball n=2 d=16: 90% error without vs 4% with; (d) disconnected double disk n=2 d=16: 118% vs 19%.
findings.source: M. Tacchi, J. B. Lasserre, D. Henrion, arXiv:2009.12139; published Discrete Comput. Geom. (2023), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00454-022-00462-0
findings.notes: Numbers extracted from ar5iv full text (https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2009.12139). Practical takeaway: even WITH Stokes, at n=2-3 and d=12-16 you get roughly 2-4 correct digits — orders of magnitude short of the 15+ digits needed for PSLQ recognition. Use moment-SOS as a sanity cross-check, not as the digit engine.

findings.claim: Sparsity-exploiting version (Tacchi, Weisser, Lasserre, Henrion, 'Exploiting Sparsity for Semi-Algebraic Set Volume Computation', arXiv:1902.02976): correlative-sparsity decomposition makes SDP relaxations much smaller and decouples subproblems. Reported examples: bicylinder n=3 (d up to 7, 0.9-18.3 s, Mosek); nonconvex n=5 set with exact volume vol K = (1/15)(7-4*sqrt(2)) ~ 0.0895 (dense d=12 relaxation ~1000 s vs sparse d=12 <10 s); polytope x_i+x_{i+1}<=1 at n=20, d=28, <100 s (true vol ~1.522e-4); chained nonconvex set x_i*x_{i+1}<=1/2 up to n=100 at d=16 in ~4 minutes.
findings.source: M. Tacchi, T. Weisser, J. B. Lasserre, D. Henrion, arXiv:1902.02976 (published in Found. Comput. Math. / journal version exists). https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.02976 ; numbers from https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1902.02976
findings.notes: Discriminant regions of low-degree polynomials in coefficient space are NOT correlatively sparse (discriminant couples all coefficients), so the n<=100 headline does not transfer; realistic dense dimension is n<=5-6.

findings.claim: Software for topic 1: GloptiPoly 3 (Matlab freeware; parses generalized problems of moments and solves via SDP) — Henrion, Lasserre, Lofberg, 'GloptiPoly 3: moments, optimization and semidefinite programming', Optimization Methods and Software 24(4-5):761-779, 2009, arXiv:0709.2559. SumOfSquares.jl is a JuMP extension implementing SOS reformulations (works with any JuMP SDP solver, e.g. Mosek, COSMO). TSSOS (Julia; Wang, Magron, Lasserre, arXiv:1912.08899) exploits term sparsity; secondary benchmark claim: GloptiPoly limited to about n=8, d=8 dense while TSSOS handles much larger polynomials. The Stokes-paper volume experiments themselves used YALMIP + GloptiPoly + MOSEK.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0709.2559 ; https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/10556780802699201 ; https://github.com/jump-dev/SumOfSquares.jl ; https://arxiv.org/pdf/1912.08899
findings.notes: GloptiPoly venue/pages verified via T&F listing. TSSOS journal venue (SIAM J. Optim. 31(1), 2021) from memory — 'likely'. Volume computation is not a built-in one-liner in any of these; you encode the moment LP with Stokes constraints manually (the Tacchi et al. papers give the formulation).

findings.claim: Mathematica's CylindricalDecomposition[expr, {x1,x2,...}] decomposes a semialgebraic region into cylindrical cells whose bounds 'in general involve algebraic functions'; ImplicitRegion works inside Integrate; Integrate[f, {x,y,...} \in reg] integrates over such regions. Combined, this enables EXACT iterated integration of 1 over a discriminant-defined region: CAD produces nested algebraic-function bounds, then Integrate evaluates the iterated integral in closed form when it can.
findings.source: Wolfram Language documentation: https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/CylindricalDecomposition.html , https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/ImplicitRegion.html.en , https://reference.wolfram.com/language/ref/Integrate.html
findings.notes: Doc statements confirmed via search snippets of the official pages. Mathematica's CAD implementation is by Adam Strzebonski (development from ~2000; 'Cylindrical algebraic decomposition using local projections', J. Symbolic Computation / ISSAC 2014, reduces cell counts). No published example of an exact discriminant-region VOLUME for degree >= 4 was found in this session — this appears to be genuinely open/undocumented territory.

findings.claim: QEPCAD B (C. W. Brown, 'QEPCAD B: A system for computing with semi-algebraic sets via cylindrical algebraic decomposition', ACM SIGSAM Bulletin, 2003) is the standard open-source CAD/quantifier-elimination system; SageMath ships an interface to it (sage.interfaces.qepcad). QEPCAD does decomposition and QE only — it does NOT integrate; you must feed its cell descriptions to a separate exact integrator.
findings.source: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/238799705_QEPCAD_B_A_system_for_computing_with_semi-algebraic_sets_via_cylindrical_algebraic_decomposition
findings.notes: Existence and title verified via listing; exact venue details (SIGSAM Bull. 37(4):97-108) and the Sage interface from background knowledge, not re-verified this session.

findings.claim: Dahlqvist, Bandukara, Omidvari, 'Exact Evaluation of Probabilistic Programs with Cylindrical Algebraic Decomposition' (arXiv:2606.24514, 2026): computes the EXACT output distribution of small programs with random inputs (arithmetic, square roots, if-else) by recasting the problem 'as a cylindrical algebraic decomposition problem followed by symbolic and/or numerical integration'. This is a direct methodological template for P(disc >= 0) with uniform inputs: CAD of the event region in the input hypercube, then exact integration cell by cell.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.24514
findings.notes: Abstract quoted from arXiv. Which CAD engine/integrator they use was not extractable from the abstract page — check full PDF in synthesis step.

findings.claim: Worked exact discriminant-region volume, quadratic case: for a x^2 + b x + c with a,b,c i.i.d. U(0,1), P(b^2 >= 4ac) = (5 + 3 ln 4)/36 = (5 + 6 ln 2)/36 ~ 0.25441; for i.i.d. U(-theta,theta) coefficients the probability is ~0.627 (independent of theta by scaling). Secondary sources state the 25.4% and 62.7% values; the (5+3 ln 4)/36 closed form re-derived independently in this session by exact iterated integration: P = int_0^1 (b^2/4)(1 - ln(b^2/4)) db = (1/4)[(1+ln 4)/3 + 2/9] = (5 + 3 ln 4)/36.
findings.source: Secondary: 'On the Probability of Real Roots in a Quadratic Equation with Coefficients as i.i.d U(-theta,theta) Variates' (Hill Publishing) https://wap.hillpublisher.com/ArticleDetails.aspx?cid=527 ; 'On the Probability of Real Roots of a Quadratic Equation when the Coefficients are iid Uniform (alpha,beta) Variates', J. Indian Soc. Probab. Stat. (2023), https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s41096-023-00149-6 ; C. Boucher, 'The probability certain random quadratics have real roots', Mathematical Gazette 105(564), 2021
findings.notes: Springer article paywalled (redirect blocked fetch); Boucher Gazette article confirmed to exist (title/author/year/volume verified on Cambridge Core) but formulas behind paywall. math.stackexchange.com is unfetchable from this environment (WebFetch blocked), so the classic MSE thread could not be quoted. The closed form itself is standard and my derivation is elementary; treat as reliable but attribute carefully in write-up.

findings.claim: KEY TOOL — Lairez, Mezzarobba, Safey El Din, 'Computing the volume of compact semi-algebraic sets' (ISSAC 2019, Beijing; arXiv:1904.11705): given a compact basic semialgebraic set S with rational coefficients, their algorithm returns vol(S) at absolute precision 2^-p in time essentially LINEAR in p — precisely 'O(p log(p)^{3+eps}) (for any eps>0) as p -> infinity' for a fixed set. Method: realize the volume as a period of a rational integral; compute a univariate Picard-Fuchs ODE by creative telescoping (Lairez 2016 Griffiths-Dwork implementation; Bostan et al. 2013); solve the ODE with the RIGOROUS numerical analytic-continuation solver of the SageMath package ore_algebra, which 'computes an interval of width O(2^-p)' with interval arithmetic throughout (their Proposition 12). Worked example: solid torus (major radius 2, minor radius 1) in R^3: volume output 39.4784176043[...]25056533975 +/- 1e-60 (= 4 pi^2); Picard-Fuchs computed in ~2 s on a laptop, ODE solved to 60 digits in <1 s, 1000 digits in under a minute.
findings.source: P. Lairez, M. Mezzarobba, M. Safey El Din, ISSAC 2019; arXiv:1904.11705, https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.11705 ; full text https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/1904.11705 ; PDF https://marc.mezzarobba.net/papers/LairezMezzarobbaSafey_Volumes_v1_2019.pdf
findings.notes: This is the single most important toolbox item found: it is rigorous (ball arithmetic end-to-end after exact symbolic preprocessing), high precision (hundreds-thousands of digits), and designed exactly for our problem class (volume of {disc >= 0} intersect hypercube is such a period). 1000 rigorous digits is vastly more than PSLQ needs. The abstract explicitly contrasts with 'exponential-time' Monte-Carlo/moment approaches. Paper does NOT itself discuss PSLQ recognition — combining the two is our synthesis. Practical dependency chain: SageMath + ore_algebra (Mezzarobba) + Lairez's periods/creative-telescoping code.

findings.claim: Follow-up: Ramesh, Weiss, 'Exact Volumes of Semi-Algebraic Convex Bodies' (ISSAC 2026; arXiv:2602.04707, submitted 2026-02-04, revised 2026-05-14): for convex bodies given by inequalities of concave polynomials, builds on Lairez-Mezzarobba-Safey El Din; 'convexity allows us to reduce the required number of creative telescoping steps by an exponential factor'; introduces a novel method to identify relevant critical values; provides 'an implementation based on the ore_algebra package in SageMath' with examples in dimensions 2, 3 and 4.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.04707 ; ACM DOI https://doi.org/10.1145/3815436.3815478
findings.notes: Discriminant regions are generally non-convex, so the exponential speedup may not apply directly, but this paper is evidence the LMS pipeline is alive, implemented, and public (ore_algebra-based code to reuse/adapt). Related: 'Computing the Hausdorff Boundary Measure of Semialgebraic Sets', SIAM J. Applied Algebra and Geometry (arXiv:2001.07598) for boundary measures via moments.

findings.claim: Arb (Fredrik Johansson) is a C library for arbitrary-precision midpoint-radius ('ball') interval arithmetic — F. Johansson, 'Arb: Efficient Arbitrary-Precision Midpoint-Radius Interval Arithmetic', IEEE Transactions on Computers 66(8), 2017 (DOI 10.1109/TC.2017.2690633; arXiv:1611.02831). Its rigorous integration ('Numerical Integration in Arbitrary-Precision Ball Arithmetic', ICMS 2018 proceedings, Springer LNCS chapter 978-3-319-96418-8_30; arXiv:1802.07942) uses the Petras algorithm: adaptive bisection + adaptive Gauss-Legendre quadrature with error bounds obtained from complex magnitudes, no derivative evaluation, giving 'rapid convergence for piecewise complex analytic integrals' and rigorous enclosures; often outperforms non-rigorous software. Accessible from Python via python-flint (arb/acb types, acb integration) — already the pinned stack in this project's eigenvalue campaign.
findings.source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.02831 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.07942 ; https://arblib.org/ ; https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-319-96418-8_30
findings.notes: python-flint wrapping claim is from project experience, not re-verified online this session. Caveat for our use: the boundary of {disc >= 0} induces sqrt-type endpoint singularities in fiber-length integrands; Petras handles piecewise ANALYTIC integrands rapidly, but non-analytic interior points degrade it — standard fix is to split at the algebraic endpoints (locate them rigorously by interval root isolation) and apply a desingularizing substitution (e.g. t = u^2) so the integrand becomes analytic. The exact convergence statement for non-analytic integrands in arXiv:1802.07942 could not be extracted from the abstract — pull from full text in synthesis.

findings.claim: IntervalArithmetic.jl (Luis Benet, UNAM and David P. Sanders, UNAM; JuliaIntervals org) is an IEEE 1788-2015-compliant Julia library for validated numerics: all quantities are intervals propagated through computations, final result is a rigorous enclosure. It underlies the JuliaIntervals ecosystem (formerly ValidatedNumerics.jl meta-package); set-inversion/paving functionality lives in companion packages (IntervalConstraintProgramming.jl / IntervalBox pavings).
findings.source: https://github.com/JuliaIntervals/IntervalArithmetic.jl ; https://juliaintervals.github.io/IntervalArithmetic.jl/dev/intro/
findings.notes: IEEE 1788-2015 compliance and authorship verified from docs. The paving/SIVIA companion-package detail is 'likely' (background knowledge).

findings.claim: SIVIA — Set Inversion Via Interval Analysis (Jaulin and Walter, 1993, introduced for guaranteed nonlinear parameter estimation; canonical book: Jaulin, Kieffer, Didrit, Walter, 'Applied Interval Analysis', Springer 2001) brackets a set S between inner and outer subpavings (unions of non-overlapping boxes) to arbitrary precision via branch-and-bound + interval tests. Known limitation quoted from the literature: 'The computational cost of this method increases exponentially concerning the dimension of the state space... SIVIA fails when the dimension of the state space is 5 or higher, even when the shape of the pre-image is simple.'
findings.source: L. Jaulin, E. Walter, 'Set inversion via interval analysis for nonlinear bounded-error estimation', Automatica 29(4):1053-1064 (1993); quote via secondary survey found in search (e.g. arXiv:2204.02241 and SIVIA implementation paper, Reliable Computing 16:239-251, https://interval.louisiana.edu/reliable-computing-journal/volume-16/reliable-computing-16-pp-239-251.pdf)
findings.notes: The 'fails at dimension >= 5' sentence is a secondary source's assessment, not Jaulin's own. Convergence analysis (mine, standard box-counting, mark as analysis not literature): with box size h in dimension d, undecided boxes concentrate on the boundary, count ~ C*h^{-(d-1)}, outer-inner volume gap ~ (boundary area)*h; with N boxes under adaptive refinement, gap ~ N^{-1/(d-1)} — i.e. O(1/N) in 2D, O(N^{-1/2}) in 3D, hopeless for many digits. Lipschitz/mean-value forms and monotonicity tests only improve the constant (decide sign on boxes at distance >~ h from the boundary in one evaluation); they cannot beat the O(h) boundary term for indicator integration. Conclusion: pure subdivision certifies ~3-6 digits in 2D-3D; use it for cross-validation, and get digits by reducing one dimension to rigorous 1D quadrature of algebraic fiber-lengths (Arb), or by the period/ODE method.

findings.claim: PSLQ precision rule (Bailey-Broadhurst, 'Parallel Integer Relation Detection: Techniques and Applications', Math. Comp. / arXiv:math/9905048): 'If one wishes to recover a relation of length n, with coefficients of maximum size d digits, then the input vector x must be specified to at least nd digits, and one must employ floating-point arithmetic accurate to at least nd digits.' Double precision only recovers 2-3-digit coefficients for n up to ~5. Detection signal: when a relation is found the smallest entry of the y-vector 'abruptly drops to roughly epsilon (i.e. 10^-p...)'; 'A drop of 20 or more orders of magnitude almost always indicates a real relation.' Foundational analysis: Ferguson, Bailey, Arno, 'Analysis of PSLQ, an integer relation finding algorithm', Mathematics of Computation 68(225):351-369, 1999.
findings.notes: Quotes obtained via search-result extraction from the paper text. Implication for our project: 15 digits supports only very small relations (e.g. n=3 basis, coefficients up to ~5 digits); a serious closed-form hunt over a basis like {1, ln 2, pi, pi^2, sqrt(2), Gamma-values, elliptic periods} with 3-digit coefficients needs 40-100+ digits — obtainable rigorously via the Lairez-Mezzarobba-Safey El Din period route, NOT via subdivision or moment-SOS.

findings.claim: mpmath.identify(x, constants=[], tol=None, maxcoeff=1000, full=False, verbose=False) 'should be used with high precision; preferably 50 digits or more'; tol 'defaults to 3/4 of the working precision'. It searches: fractions; quadratic algebraic numbers; rational linear combinations of base constants; the same after transformations 1/x, sqrt(x), x^2, log(x), exp(x) (optionally multiplied/divided by base constants); and products of fractional powers of base constants and small integers. Documented warning: at low precision it produces spurious results ('At standard precision it finds a not too useful approximation' for pi). mpmath.pslq(x, tol=None, maxcoeff=1000, maxsteps=100, verbose=False) finds integer relations; examples: pslq([-1, pi], tol=0.01) -> [22, 7]; tol=0.001 -> [355, 113]; docs note that for high-degree polynomial (minpoly-style) searches 'high precision and strict tolerance is necessary... otherwise unwanted low-accuracy approximations will be detected.'
findings.source: mpmath documentation, Number identification chapter: https://mpmath.org/doc/current/identification.html
findings.notes: Quoted from official docs. Practice recommendation: compute the volume to >=100 rigorous digits, run identify() at mp.dps ~ digits with a curated constants list (pi, ln 2, sqrt of small integers, Gamma(1/3), Gamma(1/4), lemniscate/elliptic constants, Catalan), then CONFIRM any hit by recomputing the candidate closed form to full precision and, ideally, re-deriving symbolically. Alternative/legacy: the Inverse Symbolic Calculator; for algebraic-number hunting use PARI/GP lindep/algdep or Sage's algdep (LLL-based) as an independent cross-check of PSLQ.

findings.claim: Recommended toolchain synthesis (our analysis, grounded in the above): (1) DIGIT ENGINE: Lairez-Mezzarobba-Safey El Din period/Picard-Fuchs pipeline in SageMath with ore_algebra's rigorous analytic continuation — rigorous, essentially linear in precision p, demonstrated 1000 digits in under a minute on a 3D example; adapt the ISSAC 2026 convex-bodies implementation where possible. (2) EXACT ROUTE for low degree: Mathematica CylindricalDecomposition + exact Integrate over CAD cells (worked for the quadratic case giving (5+3 ln 4)/36; feasibility for quartic+ discriminants unknown/open). (3) INDEPENDENT RIGOROUS CROSS-CHECK at 5-10 digits: interval subdivision (python-flint/Arb, this project's existing pinned stack, or IntervalArithmetic.jl) with dimension reduction to 1D Arb quadrature of algebraic fiber integrands, splitting at rigorously isolated algebraic endpoints; expect ~N^{-1/(d-1)} for naive paving, far better after fiber reduction. (4) SANITY CHECK at 2-4 digits: moment-SOS with Stokes constraints (GloptiPoly/Mosek or SumOfSquares.jl/TSSOS) which additionally provides one-sided bounds. (5) RECOGNITION: mpmath.identify/pslq at >=50-100 digits, nd-digit precision rule, demand a >=20-order-of-magnitude residual drop, then verify symbolically.

findings.notes: The individual load-bearing facts are verified above; the pipeline composition is this session's recommendation, not a published procedure.

findings.claim: CLAIM 1, value check: For x^3+px+q with (p,q) uniform on [-1,1]^2, P(three real roots) = 2*sqrt(3)/45 = 2/(15*sqrt(3)) = 0.0769800358919501 EXACTLY. Derivation (independently verified this session by exact integration): region is 4p^3+27q^2 <= 0, i.e. p<0 and |q| <= 2(-p)^{3/2}/(3*sqrt(3)); the cusp curve reaches max |q| = 2/(3*sqrt(3)) = 2*sqrt(3)/9 ~ 0.3849 < 1 at p=-1, so it never clips the square; area = int_0^1 2*(2/(3*sqrt(3)))*u^{3/2} du = 8/(15*sqrt(3)) = 8*sqrt(3)/45 ~ 0.307920; P = area/4 = 2*sqrt(3)/45. Monte Carlo with 20,000,000 samples gave 0.0770007, consistent.
findings.source: Own exact computation + Monte Carlo (Python, this session); no primary published source located stating this exact constant despite multiple targeted searches
findings.notes: Verification is of the mathematical value itself, not of an attribution. The formula 2*sqrt(3)/45 is CORRECT for this problem.

findings.claim: CLAIM 2, U(0,1) full quadratic: For a x^2+b x+c with a,b,c iid U(0,1), P(real roots) = P(b^2 >= 4ac) = (5+6*ln 2)/36 = (5+3*ln 4)/36 = 0.25441341898221310... Derivation (verified this session): for t in [0,1], P(ac <= t) = t(1-ln t); P = int_0^1 (b^2/4)(1-ln(b^2/4)) db = (1/4)[(1/3)(1+2 ln 2) + 2/9] = (5+6 ln 2)/36, using int_0^1 b^2 ln b db = -1/9. Monte Carlo 20M samples: 0.25441565. The claimed decimal 0.2544134190 is this value rounded to 10 digits.

findings.claim: CLAIM 3 CONFIRMED (primary source read in full): Hetzel, Liew & Morrison, 'The Probability that a Matrix of Integers Is Diagonalizable', Amer. Math. Monthly 114 (June-July 2007) 491-499. Theorem 3.1: for 2x2 matrices with integer entries in [-k,k], lim_{k->inf} D_2^R(k)/T_2(k) = 49/72 (the paper prints '49/72 (~68.056%)'). Remark 3.2(a) extends it verbatim to the continuous case: the probability that a 2x2 matrix with real entries (equivalently entries iid U[-1,1], via (1/16) * quadruple integral of F over [-1,1]^4) is diagonalizable over R 'is also 49/72'. Derivation quoted from the proof: eigenvalues are real precisely when (x-w)^2+4yz >= 0; partitioning by signs of y,z: cases y,z>=0 and y,z<=0 each contribute 1/4; each of the 4 mixed-sign sub-cases evaluates to 13/288 via (1/16) int_{-1}^0 int_0^1 int_{-1}^{1-sqrt(-4yz)} int_{w+sqrt(-4yz)}^1 1 dx dw dy dz = 13/288; total 2*(1/4) + 4*(13/288) = 49/72.
findings.source: Hetzel, Liew, Morrison, Amer. Math. Monthly 114 (2007) 491-499; PDF read in full from https://aimath.org/~morrison/Research/diagmat.pdf
findings.notes: 49/72 = 0.680555... Nuance for the synthesis: the paper's headline Theorem 3.1 is about integer matrices (natural density as k->inf); the iid-U[-1,1] statement is Remark 3.2(a), where it follows by scale invariance from the same integral. Diagonalizable-over-R and all-eigenvalues-real coincide in the limit by their Corollary 2.2 / measure-zero repeated eigenvalues.

findings.claim: CLAIM 3 cross-quote CONFIRMED (primary source read in full): Martin & Wong, 'The number of 2x2 integer matrices having a prescribed integer eigenvalue', arXiv:0808.1922v1 [math.PR] (14 Aug 2008), Introduction: 'An explicit calculation by Hetzel, Liew, and Morrison [4] shows that a 2x2 matrix with entries independently chosen uniformly from [-1,1] has real eigenvalues with probability 49/72.' Repeated on p.3: 'For M_2([-1,1]) we are conditioning on having real eigenvalues, which occurs with probability 49/72 (this can be obtained by integrating W(delta)...; the computation by Hetzel, Liew, and Morrison [4] is more direct).' Their Theorem 3 also gives the explicit piecewise density W(delta) (with log terms, supported on |delta|<=2, W(1)=15/32, maxima at delta ~ +/-0.75030751) for real eigenvalues of 2x2 U[-1,1] matrices — a richer anchor than the single number.

findings.claim: CLAIM 4 CONFIRMED (primary source read in full): Alan Edelman, 'The Circular Law and the Probability that a Random Matrix Has k Real Eigenvalues' (preprint dated March 23, 1993, UC Berkeley; published as 'The probability that a random real Gaussian matrix has k real eigenvalues, related distributions, and the circular law', J. Multivariate Anal. 60 (1997), no. 2, 203-232). Abstract: 'Let A be an n by n matrix whose elements are independent random variables with standard normal distributions... we show that the probability that A has all real eigenvalues is exactly 2^{-n(n-1)/4}.' Main-results box: 'The probability p_{n,k} that a random A has k real eigenvalues has the form r + s*sqrt(2), where r and s are rational. In particular... p_{n,n} = 1/2^{n(n-1)/4}' (Cor 7.1 and 7.2). Corollary 7.1 proof: 'When k = n and l = 0, d_{n,n} = 2^{n(n-1)/4} and the integrand is simply 1' — the constant falls directly out of the real-Schur-decomposition Jacobian (Theorem 5.1) integrated against the Gaussian density.
findings.source: Edelman preprint PDF read in full from https://math.mit.edu/~edelman/homepage/papers/circular.pdf; published citation J. Multivariate Anal. 60 (1997) 203-232
findings.notes: Precise statement: n x n, entries iid standard normal N(0,1); P(all n eigenvalues real) = 2^{-n(n-1)/4}. Sanity anchors from the paper's exact table: p_{2,2} = sqrt(2)/2 ~ 0.70711 (= 2^{-1/2}), p_{3,3} = sqrt(2)/4 ~ 0.35355, p_{4,4} = 1/8, p_{5,5} = 1/32, p_{6,6} = sqrt(2)/256 ~ 0.00552. Paper also notes Theorem 6.1 (joint density) was independently found by Lehmann & Sommers, Phys. Rev. Lett. 67 (1991) 941-944.

findings.source: A. Edelman, 'The probability that a random real Gaussian matrix has k real eigenvalues, related distributions, and the circular law', Journal of Multivariate Analysis 60(2):203-232 (1997); cited with full bibliographic detail in MO 372115 body (core.ac.uk/download/pdf/82140233.pdf)
findings.notes: Formula independently quoted in multiple primary abstracts fetched (e.g. arXiv:1503.07926 context, MSE comments).

findings.claim: Exact 2x2 results for non-Gaussian entries (the only rigorous fixed-n non-Gaussian values found anywhere, 2015): for 2x2 matrices with i.i.d. zero-mean entries, P(both eigenvalues real) is: UNIFORM on [-1,1]: 49/72 ≈ 0.680556 (their Eq. 16); Gaussian: 1/sqrt(2) ≈ 0.7071; Laplace: 11/15 ≈ 0.7333; Cauchy: 3/4 = 0.75. General formula (their Eq. 5): P = 1 - 4∫_0^u dx ∫_0^u dy ∫_0^{2sqrt(xy)} dz q(z)p(x)p(y), where p is the entry density and q = p*p (self-convolution); Fourier version in their Eq. 9. Abstract verbatim: 'Within the class of smooth distributions with zero mean and finite variance, our results indicate that the Gaussian distribution has the maximum probability of real eigenvalues, but the Cauchy distribution characterised by infinite variance is found to have a larger probability of real eigenvalues than the normal. We also find that for the two-dimensional single matrices, the probability of real eigenvalues lies in the range [5/8,7/8].'
findings.source: S. Hameed, K. Jain, A. Lakshminarayan, 'Real eigenvalues of non-Gaussian random matrices and their products', J. Phys. A: Math. Theor. 48, 385204 (2015); arXiv:1504.06256 (abstract fetched verbatim; equation-level values from ar5iv full-text fetch)
findings.notes: Abstract quoted verbatim from arxiv.org/abs/1504.06256v4. Equation numbers (5), (9), (16) and the Laplace/Cauchy values are from a full-text fetch via ar5iv (secondary rendering) — mark equation numbers 'likely'. This 2x2 computation is EXACTLY the coefficient-space method: P(disc >= 0) with disc = (a-d)^2 + 4bc, computed through the joint law of (a-d, bc). Crucially it proves fixed-n all-real probabilities are NOT universal (49/72 != 1/sqrt(2)).

findings.claim: Universality of the expected NUMBER of real eigenvalues (Tao-Vu): a real n x n matrix whose entries are jointly independent, exponentially decaying, and whose moments match the real Gaussian ensemble to fourth order has sqrt(2n/pi) + o(sqrt(n)) real eigenvalues asymptotically almost surely (matches Edelman-Kostlan-Shub's Gaussian asymptotic E N_R ~ sqrt(2n/pi)).
findings.source: T. Tao, V. Vu, 'Random matrices: Universality of local spectral statistics of non-Hermitian matrices', Annals of Probability 43(2):782-874 (2015); arXiv:1206.1893 (abstract fetched)
findings.notes: Fourth-moment matching EXCLUDES U[0,1] (nonzero mean) and does not directly match centered uniform (4th moment of normalized uniform is 9/5, Gaussian is 3) — so Tao-Vu does not literally cover uniform entries; it covers e.g. specially tuned distributions. Relevant as the universality baseline the question's asymptotics would plug into.

findings.claim: Number-of-real-eigenvalues fluctuations and transitions (2016): for a wide class of matrices the number k_n of real eigenvalues of an n x n matrix is asymptotically Gaussian with mean k̄_n = O(sqrt(n)) and variance k̄_n(2-sqrt(2)); the limit distribution of real eigenvalues transitions from bimodal for k_n = o(sqrt(n)) to unimodal for k_n = O(n), uniform at the transition; predicted via log-gas in Ginibre and shown NUMERICALLY to hold 'for a wide range of random matrices with independent entries beyond the universality class of the circular law'.
findings.source: L. C. García del Molino, K. Pakdaman, J. Touboul, 'Real eigenvalues of non-symmetric random matrices: Transitions and Universality', arXiv:1605.00623 (2016) (abstract fetched verbatim)

findings.claim: Probability of NO real eigenvalues (Gaussian-specific, 2016): for the real Ginibre ensemble, lim_{n→∞} (1/sqrt(2n)) log p(2n, 0 real) = -(1/sqrt(2π)) ζ(3/2), ζ the Riemann zeta function.

findings.claim: Products of random matrices with GENERAL i.i.d. entries: it is conjectured that P(A_1 A_2 ... A_n has all real eigenvalues) → 1 as n → ∞ for i.i.d. k x k factors with entries i.i.d. from any probability measure μ; proven when μ has an atom. Abstract verbatim: 'Then it is conjectured that P(X_n has all real eigenvalues) → 1 as n → ∞. We show that the conjecture is true when μ has an atom.'

findings.notes: Hameed-Jain-Lakshminarayan (2015) gave the numerical evidence for this phenomenon across distributions and showed entry correlations (not marginals) drive the approach to 1.

findings.claim: Part 3 (entry space → coefficient space): NO published work was found computing the joint density of (trace, second elementary symmetric function e2, determinant) — equivalently the characteristic-polynomial coefficient vector — for i.i.d. uniform 3x3 matrices. Multiple targeted searches (joint distribution of char-poly coefficients for uniform entries; exact determinant density for 3x3 uniform) returned only: determinant MOMENT literature, Nguyen-Vu-type results for Bernoulli determinants, mod-Gaussian convergence for random determinants (arXiv:1707.00449), and secular-determinant work for unitary matrices — nothing on the trivariate joint law. The nearest existing instances of the method are (a) Hameed et al's 2x2 computation, which is precisely P(disc >= 0) pushed through the joint law of coefficient combinations, and (b) the MSE 5054093 comment thread (Srini + Exodd, Jan 2026): expanding disc(charpoly) as a homogeneous degree-6 polynomial in the 9 entries yields ~210 monomial terms drawn from ~9 distinct product-PDF types; Srini proposes computing exact means/variances of the terms and a normal approximation for P(disc > 0); Exodd notes even just the variance of the discriminant would give Markov/Chebyshev-type bounds. Nobody has carried this out.
findings.source: Absence established by searches on 2026-08-17 (web + arXiv); the 210-term discussion: comments on https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/5054093/ retrieved verbatim via API
findings.notes: For synthesis: this means the project's plan (compute the volume where disc >= 0 in coefficient space with the pushforward density of (e1,e2,e3)) has no direct prior art for uniform entries; the 2x2 convolution formula (Eq. 5/9 of arXiv:1504.06256) is the template that has been executed.

open_questions: No closed form or nontrivial bounds exist for P_3 = P(3x3 i.i.d. U[0,1] matrix has all real eigenvalues); best knowledge is Monte Carlo 0.7075950 (10^11 trials) and the near-trivial bounds (1/12)^8 <= P_3 <= 1 - 6(1/8)^9. The conjecture P_3 = 1/sqrt(2) is numerically excluded (~340 sigma).

No published value at all for the centered-uniform U[-1,1] 3x3 case; our own 2x10^8-trial run gives 0.321647 ± 0.000033 (this session, not literature) — a synthesis-step decision is whether to publish/verify this independently.

Why does P_n(U[0,1]) track Q_{n-1} = 2^{-(n-1)(n-2)/4} (real Ginibre one dimension down)? The Perron-eigenvalue deflation heuristic (comments of Hagen von Eitzen, 2021) has never been made rigorous, and the 10^11-trial n=3 value 0.70759 vs Q_2 = 0.70711 shows the match is close but NOT exact.

Is there any exact-integration attack on P_3 via the coefficient space (e1,e2,e3) = (trace, sum of 2x2 principal minors, det)? No literature computes this trivariate joint density for uniform entries; the discriminant is a degree-6 form in 9 entries (~210 monomials when expanded), and only a variance/normal-approximation sketch exists in MSE 5054093 comments (Jan 2026).

Fixed-n non-universality vs asymptotic universality: 2x2 exact values (49/72 uniform vs 1/sqrt(2) Gaussian vs 3/4 Cauchy) prove the all-real probability is distribution-dependent at fixed n, while expected real-eigenvalue COUNTS are universal asymptotically (Tao-Vu under 4-moment matching). Whether log P(all real) ~ -c n^2 holds with the SAME c = (log 2)/4 for uniform entries as for Gaussian is completely open.
Whether the Xiao et al (2022) Bernoulli sqrt(N) real-eigenvalue claim is stated in the paper body as quoted by the search snippet (not verified against the PDF).
Tao-Vu's four-moment matching does not cover uniform entries (normalized uniform has 4th moment 9/5 != 3); no universality theorem currently applies to the uniform ensembles in the question.

findings.claim: For the quadratic AX^2+BX+C=0 with A,B,C i.i.d. U(-theta,theta), the probability of real roots is 62.7% (independent of theta); with coefficients i.i.d. U(0,theta) it is 25.4%. The proof route uses P(B^2>=4AC)=1 whenever AC<=0, plus direct integration otherwise; verified in the paper by Monte Carlo.
findings.source: Subhomoy Haldar, Soubhik Chakraborty, "On the Probability of Real Roots in a Quadratic Equation with Coefficients as i.i.d U(-theta,theta) Variates", Journal of Applied Mathematics and Computation (Hill Publishing), 2021. https://wap.hillpublisher.com/ArticleDetails.aspx?cid=527
findings.notes: Numbers 62.7% and 25.4% quoted directly from the article page. The exact closed forms behind these decimals are the classical values P_{U(0,1)} = (5+6 ln 2)/36 = 5/36 + (ln 2)/6 ≈ 0.25441 and P_{U(-1,1)} = 1/2 + (1/2)(5+6 ln 2)/36 = (41+6 ln 2)/72 ≈ 0.62719; I re-derived both by direct integration and they match the paper's percentages, but I could not see the closed forms printed in the paper itself (label the closed-form attribution 'likely').

U(0,1), P(real roots) = 1/12; classical non-monic U(0,1) case P = (5+6 ln 2)/36 ≈ 0.2544. For the depressed cubic x^3+px+q with p,q i.i.d. U(-1,1), P(three real roots) = area{4p^3+27q^2<=0}/4 = 2*sqrt(3)/45 ≈ 0.07698.

findings.claim: DPSZ theorem (foundational asymptotics): for a degree-n polynomial with i.i.d. zero-mean coefficients with all moments finite, P(exactly k real zeros) = n^{-b+o(1)} as n->infty through integers of the parity of k; b is characterized via the centered stationary Gaussian process with correlation function sech(t/2); b depends neither on k nor on the coefficient law; with nonzero-mean coefficients the exponent becomes b/2.
findings.source: A. Dembo, B. Poonen, Q.-M. Shao, O. Zeitouni, "Random polynomials having few or no real zeros", J. Amer. Math. Soc. 15 (2002) 857-892; arXiv:math/0006113. https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0006113
findings.notes: All statements quoted from the arXiv abstract (primary). DPSZ's numerical estimate b ≈ 0.76 appears in the paper body (not verified here directly).

findings.claim: Poplavskyi & Schehr proved the exact persistence exponent theta(2) = 3/16 for the 2d diffusion equation with random initial condition, and deduced that the probability q_0(n) that a Kac polynomial of (even) degree n has NO real root decays as q_0(n) ~ n^{-3/4}. This settles the DPSZ constant for no-real-root persistence: b = 3/4.
findings.source: Mihail Poplavskyi, Gregory Schehr, "Exact persistence exponent for the 2d-diffusion equation and related Kac polynomials", 2018, arXiv:1806.11275 (published PRL 121, 150601 (2018)). https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.11275
findings.notes: theta(2)=3/16 and q_0(n) ~ n^{-3/4} quoted from the arXiv abstract. Earlier physics treatment of the diffusion/Kac connection: G. Schehr, S. N. Majumdar, "Real Roots of Random Polynomials and Zero Crossing Properties of Diffusion Equation", J. Stat. Phys. (2008), arXiv:0803.4396, which also gives decay rates exp(-2 theta_inf sqrt(n)) (Weyl) and exp(-pi theta_inf sqrt(n)/...) (binomial/Kostlan) for no-real-root probabilities of other ensembles (secondary wording from search summary).

findings.claim: Large-deviation route to P(all roots real) for general degree: Zeitouni-Zelditch proved an LDP for the empirical measure of zeros of Gaussian random polynomials with SPEED N^2 and rate function given by a weighted energy functional on CP^1 (IMRN 2010, 20, 3939-3992); Butez (EJP 21 (2016), arXiv:1509.09136) extended it to real Gaussian coefficients; Butez-Zeitouni (ECP 22 (2017), arXiv:1607.02392) proved UNIVERSALITY for i.i.d. coefficients possessing a density w.r.t. Lebesgue on C, R, or R+ (density not vanishing too fast at 0, tail decay at least exp(-|x|^rho)). Uniform coefficients satisfy these hypotheses, so P(all roots real) for the project's ensemble should decay as exp(-cN^2) with an ensemble-independent constant given by the rate function — but I could NOT verify an explicit 'all roots real' corollary in any of the three papers' accessible text.

Zelditch, "Large deviations of empirical measures of zeros of random polynomials", IMRN 2010:20, 3939-3992 (preprint https://cims.nyu.edu/~zeitouni/pdf/LDRSg0Dec0909.pdf); R. Butez, arXiv:1509.09136 / EJP 10.1214/16-EJP5; R. Butez, O. Zeitouni, arXiv:1607.02392 / ECP (2017), https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ecp/1483952415

findings.claim: Random-matrix analog with exact answer: the probability that all eigenvalues of an n x n real Ginibre matrix (i.i.d. N(0,1) entries) are real is exactly 2^{-n(n-1)/4} (Edelman 1997). For n=3 this gives 2^{-3/2} ≈ 0.35355. For the uniform-entry analog no closed form is known.

findings.claim: Forrester extended the all-real-eigenvalues probability to PRODUCTS of m standard Gaussian matrices: p^{P_m}_{N,N} equals an (N/2)x(N/2) (N even) or ((N+1)/2)x((N+1)/2) (N odd) determinant with Meijer G-function entries; for large N, p^{P_m}_{N,N} ~ b_m^{N^2} with explicit b_m; for m=2 the leading decay is (pi/4)^{N^2/2}; and p^{P_m}_{N,N} -> 1 as m -> infinity for fixed N.
findings.source: Peter J. Forrester, "Probability of all eigenvalues real for products of standard Gaussian matrices", J. Phys. A 47 (2014) 065202, arXiv:1309.7736. https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.7736

findings.claim: Exact volumes of coefficient regions defined by root-location constraints exist in the literature via Selberg-type integrals: (i) DiPippo-Howe compute the volume of the set V_n of coefficient vectors of monic real degree-2n polynomials with all roots on the unit circle; (ii) the Akiyama-Petho / Kirschenhofer-Weitzer line computes Lebesgue measures v_d^{(s)} of monic degree-d 'contractive' polynomials (all roots in unit disc) with exactly s complex-conjugate pairs — in particular v_d^{(0)} is the volume of the totally-real region — and proves v_d^{(1)}/v_d^{(0)} = (P_d(3)-2d-1)/4 where P_d = Legendre polynomial, with all ratios v_d^{(s)}/v_d^{(0)} integers.
findings.source: S. A. DiPippo, E. W. Howe, "Real polynomials with all roots on the unit circle and abelian varieties over finite fields", J. Number Theory 73 (1998), arXiv:math/9803097; P. Kirschenhofer, M. Weitzer, "A number theoretic problem on the distribution of polynomials with bounded roots", arXiv:1405.1530 (2014); S. Akiyama, A. Petho, "On the distribution of polynomials with bounded roots I, II" (I: real coefficients; II: with Galois symmetry).
findings.notes: DiPippo-Howe scope and the Kirschenhofer-Weitzer Legendre formula quoted from arXiv abstracts (verified). Akiyama-Petho series existence is secondary (cited context). The Jacobian |Vandermonde| / Selberg-integral technique used in these papers is exactly the map roots->coefficients volume computation relevant to the project.

findings.claim: Frank Calegari's Persiflage blog posts 'Thurston, Selberg, and Random Polynomials' (Parts I & II, May 2014) work out coefficient-space volumes for monic degree-N polynomials with all roots real in [-1,1] via Vandermonde/Selberg integrals: C_{N,0}(T,alpha) = (1/N!) int_{[-1,1]^N} |prod x_i|^{alpha-1} prod (T-x_i) prod |x_i-x_j| dx; derived facts include: probability that the largest root is real, conditional on all roots in [-1,1], equals 1/N (N odd) and 1/(N-1) (N even); expected number of real roots of a polynomial conditioned to have all roots of modulus <=1 is ~ (1/pi) log N; motivated by Thurston's experiment (arXiv:1402.2008, 'Entropy in dimension one') sampling 20000 degree-21 polynomials with coefficients in [-5,5] and extracting Perron polynomials.

Calegari, Persiflage blog, Part I: https://galoisrepresentations.wordpress.com/2014/05/21/thurston-selberg-and-random-polynomials-part-i/ , Part II: https://galoisrepresentations.wordpress.com/2014/05/24/thurston-selberg-and-random-polynomials-part-ii/ (also mirrored in "PERSIFLAGE: MATH BLOG POSTS" PDF, http://www.math.uchicago.edu/~fcale/papers/blog.pdf)

Post mentions the problem was given as a thesis problem to student Zili Huang (U Chicago) — a possible thesis on real-rootedness probabilities to chase.

Kostov has an entire monograph, 'Topics on Hyperbolic Polynomials in One Variable' (SMF, Panoramas et Syntheses 33, 2011), plus papers stratifying the hyperbolicity domain by discriminant sets ('Root configurations for hyperbolic polynomials of degree 3, 4, and 5', Funct. Anal. Appl. 2002: 10 non-degenerate root/derivative-root configurations for degree 4, 116 for degree 5; Whitney property of the hyperbolicity domain of x^n + lambda_2 x^{n-2} + ...); Meguerditchian's 'Obreschkoff's theorem revisited: what convex sets are contained in the set of hyperbolic polynomials?' (J. Pure Appl. Algebra 1992) characterizes convex subsets of the hyperbolicity region.

findings.claim: Independent exact values for the iid-UNIFORM ensembles (useful benchmark data the synthesis step probably wants, since Li's own values are unrecovered): (a) Quadratic Ax^2+Bx+C, A,B,C iid U(-1,1) (equivalently U(-theta,theta)): P(real roots) = (41 + 6 ln 2)/72 = 41/72 + (ln 2)/12 ≈ 0.6272 — derived in full in Limmer 1999 pp. 19-20 (primary source, exact integration), scale-invariant so independent of theta; corroborated by the Hill Publisher paper ('62.7%') and by Andel's Q*-independent-of-n observation. (b) Quadratic with A,B,C iid U(0,theta): P(real roots) ≈ 25.4% (Hill Publisher paper; exact value 5/36 + (ln 2)/6 ≈ 0.25441 per Math.SE 1745310's quadratic aside). (c) Cubic Ax^3+Bx^2+Cx+D, coefficients iid U(-1,1): P(all three roots real) ≈ 0.21829 by Mathematica numerical integration of the discriminant-positivity region (Math.SE q.1745310, April 2016), consistent with Limmer 1999 Monte Carlo estimate 0.2178 (p. 61). No closed form known in these sources. (d) Gaussian N(0,1) iid coefficients: quadratic P(2 real) ≈ 0.6485 via Kac formula (E ≈ 1.2970); cubic P(3 real) ≈ 0.246380 (Limmer 1999 pp. 20-21, 61). (e) Kostlan ensemble (coefficient k ~ N(0, C(n,k))): E[# real roots] = sqrt(n), giving P(all real) = sqrt(2)/2 ≈ 0.70710 for quadratics and (sqrt(3)-1)/2 ≈ 0.36602 for cubics (Math.SE 1745310 citing Kostlan; see also Edelman-Kostlan BAMS 32(1):1-37, 1995).
findings.source: Limmer 1999 OSU thesis (ir.library.oregonstate.edu/downloads/6395wb245), pp. 19-21, 61-62 — primary derivations; Math.StackExchange question 1745310 'The probability that a random (real) cubic has three real roots'; Hill Publisher article 'On the Probability of Real Roots in a Quadratic Equation with Coefficients as i.i.d U(-theta,theta) Variates' (wap.hillpublisher.com/ArticleDetails.aspx?cid=527)

findings.claim: SESSION-DERIVED RESULT (not literature; produced during this search as reference data): P(monic cubic, (a,b,c) iid U[-1,1]) = 383/4860 + ln(3)/48 = 0.101694340376058869599540860131... Derivation: with t=sqrt(a^2-3b), the c-interval giving 3 real roots is [c_lo,c_hi], c_lo=(a+t)^2(a-2t)/27, c_hi=(a-t)^2(a+2t)/27, of length 4t^3/27; key lemma (verified numerically to be tight only at the corner (|a|,b)=(1,-1) where (a+t)^2(2t-a)=27 exactly): for all (a,b) in [-1,1]x[-1,a^2/3] the interval [c_lo,c_hi] lies inside [-1,1], so the cube never truncates it; hence P=(1/8)*Int_{-1}^{1}(8/405)(a^2+3)^{5/2} da = (2/405)[383/24+(135/32)ln 3] = 383/4860 + ln(3)/48.
findings.source: This session's computation (scipy dblquad, mpmath 30-digit quadrature agreeing with the closed form to all 30 digits, 100M-sample Monte Carlo consistent; no-truncation lemma verified on a 2001x2001 grid, max exactly 27.0 at the corner)

findings.claim: Historical prior art: 'Already in the seventeenth century, Waring considered random cubic polynomials and concluded that the probability of having three real roots is at most 2/3. findings.claim: Sign-condition characterization for quartic ax^4+bx^3+cx^2+dx+e: define P = 8ac - 3b^2, D = 64a^3e - 16a^2c^2 + 16ab^2c - 16a^2bd - 3b^4, Delta_0 = c^2 - 3bd + 12ae, R = b^3 + 8da^2 - 4abc, and Delta the standard 16-term degree-6 discriminant (leading terms 256a^3e^3 - 192a^2bde^2 - 128a^2c^2e^2 + 144a^2cd^2e - 27a^2d^4 + ...). All four roots are real and distinct iff Delta > 0 AND P < 0 AND D < 0. If Delta > 0 and (P > 0 OR D > 0): two pairs of complex-conjugate roots (no real roots). If Delta < 0: exactly two real roots. Delta = 0: multiple-root cases classified via Delta_0, D, R.
findings.source: Wikipedia, 'Quartic function', section 'Nature of the roots' (fetched 2026-08-17)
findings.notes: Key structural point for the 'volume where discriminant is nonnegative' framing: for quartics {Delta >= 0} strictly contains the all-real region — Delta > 0 also holds on the all-complex region, so P(all real) = vol{Delta>=0, P<=0, D<=0}, NOT vol{Delta>=0}. (For cubics Delta>=0 alone does characterize all-real.)

findings.claim: Dembo-Poonen-Shao-Zeitouni (DPSZ): for a polynomial of large degree n with iid, nondegenerate, zero-mean coefficients having finite moments of all orders, P(exactly k real zeros) = n^{-b+o(1)} as n -> infinity through integers of the parity of k; in particular P(no real zeros, n even) = n^{-b+o(1)}. b depends neither on k nor on the coefficient law. With nonzero-mean coefficients, b is replaced by b/2.
findings.source: A. Dembo, B. Poonen, Q.-M. Shao, O. Zeitouni, 'Random polynomials having few or no real zeros', J. Amer. Math. Soc. 15 (2002) 857-892; arXiv:math/0006113 (abstract + full text via ar5iv)
findings.notes: Universality class includes U(-1,1) coefficients (zero mean, all moments finite) — so for the uniform ensemble of the research project, P(no real roots) = n^{-b+o(1)}; for U(0,1) (positive mean) the exponent is b/2. The result also holds for the number of zeros being o(log n / log log n).

findings.claim: DPSZ characterization of b: b = -4 lim_{T->infinity} (1/T) log P(sup_{0<=t<=T} Y_t <= 0), where Y is the centered stationary Gaussian process with correlation function sech(t/2). Rigorous bounds: 0.4 <= b <= 2 (their Lemma 2.5; upper via Slepian vs Ornstein-Uhlenbeck). Their simulations of polynomials of degree up to ~1024 suggested b = 0.76 +/- 0.03.

findings.notes: The factor 4 encodes the four critical windows x -> 1^-, 1^+, -1^-, -1^+ of the Kac polynomial, each contributing the persistence of the sech(t/2) process in logarithmic time.

findings.claim: Schehr-Majumdar (PRL 2007): for a class of real random polynomials indexed by integer d, P(no real root in [0,1]) ~ n^{-theta(d)} where theta(d) is the persistence exponent of the diffusion equation with random initial condition in spatial dimension d; for n even, P(no root on the whole real axis) ~ n^{-2(theta(d)+theta(2))}. Standard Kac corresponds to d=2, giving n^{-4 theta(2)}.

Phys. 2008) numerical persistence exponents: theta_sim(1) = 0.12050(5); theta_sim(2) = 0.1875(1); theta_infinity = 0.417(3) (persistence exponent of the Gaussian-correlated stationary process, d->infinity limit; IIA approximation 0.411497); large-d scaling theta(d) = 2^{-3/2} theta_infinity sqrt(d). Also: P(no real root) for Weyl polynomials q_0(n) ~ exp(-2 theta_infinity sqrt(n)) and for binomial (Kostlan/SO(2)) polynomials q_0(n) ~ exp(-pi theta_infinity sqrt(n)).

findings.claim: Poplavskyi-Schehr (PRL 2018): exact persistence exponent theta(2) = 3/16 for the 2d diffusion equation with random initial condition (p_0(t) ~ t^{-3/16}); consequently the probability that Kac polynomials of (even) degree n have no real root decays as q_0(n) ~ n^{-3/4}. Derived via a connection with the truncated real orthogonal ensemble of random matrices. Hence the DPSZ constant is b = 4*(3/16) = 3/4 EXACTLY — a closed form IS known.

findings.claim: Large-deviation framework relevant to P(all n roots real): (i) Zeitouni-Zelditch prove an LDP for the empirical measure of zeros of Gaussian random polynomials (SU(2)/Kostlan-type ensembles on CP^1) with speed N^2 and rate function given by a weighted Green's-energy functional, with corollaries for hole probabilities of the form exp(-c N^2); (ii) Butez extends the LDP (speed n^2) to REAL Gaussian coefficients for Kac and elliptic polynomials; (iii) Butez-Zeitouni prove universality of the speed-n^2 LDP for iid coefficients with a density on R (density not vanishing too fast at 0, tail decay exp(-|x|^rho)) — this covers uniform([-1,1]) coefficients.

findings.claim: Exact all-real probabilities ARE known for adjacent random-matrix (not iid-coefficient) ensembles: (i) real Ginibre (N x N iid N(0,1) entries): P(all eigenvalues real) = 2^{-N(N-1)/4} (Edelman); (ii) real spherical ensemble / Gaussian real generalized eigenvalue problem det(X1 - lambda X2)=0: p_{2,2} = pi/4, p_{3,3} = 1/2, p_{4,4} = (27/1024) pi^2, with p_{N,k} a polynomial in pi of degree N/2 for even N and rational for odd N (Forrester-Mays Prop. 3.10); (iii) products of m truncated real orthogonal matrices: P(all real) is a rational number for each L_i even (Forrester et al.); (iv) elliptic real Ginibre: log p_{n,n-2l} = a1 n^2 + a2 n + a3 log n + O(1) at strong non-Hermiticity, all coefficients explicit (Akemann-Byun-Lee 2025).

novelty_verdict: OPEN / NOT PUBLISHED, with one narrow archival caveat. For P(x^3+ax^2+bx+c has 3 real roots), (a,b,c) iid U[-1,1]: no closed form and no numeric value of ANY precision has been published anywhere discoverable as of 2026-08-17. Decisive evidence: (1) MSE's and MathOverflow's own search engines (queried via proxy this session, closing the sweep's blind spot) return zero threads on the monic case; (2) the canonical MSE thread 1745310 was fetched in full and covers only the NON-monic cubic — and even there its best numeric (0.21829) is refuted at 9 sigma by this session's independent MC (true non-monic value 0.2180); (3) the only numeric ever published for any cubic-on-cube probability (0.2219, Purdue seminar slides 2012, non-monic) is wrong at the third digit — so nothing remotely 'high-precision' exists even for the easier variant; (4) exhaustive arXiv/journal/OEIS-digit/forum searches by 7 agents plus this session's digit-string searches ('383/4860', '0.10169434', etc.) found nothing; (5) the published exact literature stops at degree 2 (Haldar-Chakraborty 2021, Boucher 2021, JISPS 2023). The candidate closed form 383/4860 + ln(3)/48 = 0.101694340376058869... is a product of this sweep, now verified by two fully independent computations (agent 3: derivation + 30-digit mpmath + 100M MC; this session: antiderivative identity to 15 digits + 2x10^8 MC on the raw discriminant at -0.35 sigma + grid proof of the no-truncation lemma), with the companion U(0,1)^3 value 1/2880 confirmed at -0.05 sigma. The sole remaining pre-emption risk is Li (1988), Comm. Statist. Theory Methods 17(2):395-409 — paywalled, essentially uncited (2 citers, neither reproduces a single value), title/keywords match the monic setting, but Limmer (1999, who read it) says it used NON-uniform coefficient distributions. Recommended claim language: 'to our knowledge not previously published; the closest prior work, Li (1988), treats monic low-degree polynomials with non-uniform coefficient distributions (per Limmer 1999) and its special cases could not be inspected'. Gate a formal novelty assertion on an ILL/MathSciNet check of Li 1988 (MR 89j:60069); secondary low-risk unchecked sources: Bharucha-Reid & Sambandham 1986 (book, known to focus on E[#real zeros]), the Politecnico di Milano MSc thesis, and the paywalled quadratic papers' introductions.
